name: Bhel Puri
cuisine: Mumbai street food (Gujarati-Maharashtrian chaat; beach snack of Chowpatty and Juhu)

ingredients.name: Coriander leaves (hara dhania)
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ½ cup, loosely packed (8 g chutney, 4 g garnish)

ingredients.name: Green chilli (hari mirch)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 small (half in chutney, half chopped for the bhel)

equipment: Small saucepan for the tamarind chutney
Kadai or wide pan to dry-toast the puffed rice
Small mixer jar or mortar for the green chutney
Small pressure cooker or pot for the potato
Large mixing bowl (bigger than you think, to toss without crushing) and a spoon
Knife, chopping board, measuring spoons, kitchen scale (or use the spoon measures)

steps.title: Boil the potato
steps.text: Put 1 small potato (about 80 g, half is used) in a small pot, cover with water and boil until a knife slides in.
steps.visualCue: A knife goes into the centre with no resistance and the skin splits slightly
steps.cameraCheck: The knife piercing the boiled potato
steps.videoShot: Knife slipping into a boiled potato.
steps.watchOut: Hard centre, which is crunchy raw potato in the bhel; boil 3 min more. Overboiled potato falls apart into mush when diced, so lift it out as soon as the knife slides in.

steps.title: Mix the tamarind and jaggery
steps.text: In a small saucepan add 6 g tamarind paste, 8 g grated jaggery and 30 ml water, and stir.
steps.visualCue: The brown paste breaks up into a dark, cloudy liquid with no big lumps
steps.videoShot: Spoon pressing tamarind and jaggery into water.
steps.watchOut: Hard lumps of tamarind or jaggery, which stay sour or sweet in patches; press them against the pan with the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Simmer the chutney
steps.text: Put the pan on low-medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Small bubbles at the edge, and it coats the back of a spoon like thin syrup
steps.cameraCheck: The simmering chutney on the spoon
steps.videoShot: Chutney dripping off a spoon like thin syrup.
steps.watchOut: Boiling dry and burning the jaggery (a bitter, caramel smell, with a thick, sticky bottom); keep the flame low and add 1 tbsp water if it thickens too fast. It also thickens as it cools, so stop while it is still pourable.

steps.title: Season and cool the chutney
steps.text: Turn off the heat, stir in 0.3 g roasted cumin powder, 0.2 g chilli powder and 0.3 g black salt. Pour it into a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: A glossy brown, sweet-sour smell with a smoky edge
steps.cameraCheck: The seasoned chutney in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Spices stirred into the brown chutney.
steps.watchOut: Adding the chutney warm to the puffed rice, which makes the bhel soggy at once; let it cool to room temperature first.

steps.title: Blend the green chutney
steps.text: Put 8 g coriander leaves, 3 g mint, ½ green chilli (1.5 g), 3 ml lemon juice, a tiny pinch of salt and 1 tbsp water into a small mixer jar and blend.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, bright green paste that is pourable
steps.cameraCheck: The green chutney in a bowl
steps.videoShot: Green paste pouring off a spoon.
steps.watchOut: Too much water, which turns it thin and spreads sogginess; add water 1 tsp at a time. A dull olive colour means it was blended too long or left in the heat, so blend in short pulses.

steps.title: Toast the puffed rice
steps.text: Put 25 g puffed rice in a dry kadai on low heat and stir.
steps.tip: Spread it on a plate to cool; a hot bowl softens the sev.
steps.visualCue: The puffs feel dry and crisp, and make a light crackling sound, with no colour change
steps.cameraCheck: The toasted puffed rice on a plate
steps.videoShot: Puffed rice stirred in a dry pan.
steps.watchOut: Browning or burning, which tastes bitter (it goes very fast); take it off the heat the moment it feels hot and crisp. Soft or chewy puffs just need a longer toast.

steps.title: Chop the onion and tomato
steps.text: Finely chop 30 g onion and 30 g tomato (about 2 tbsp each). Slit and finely chop the other ½ green chilli.
steps.visualCue: Tiny, even cubes about the size of a pea or smaller
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped onion and tomato in two small bowls
steps.videoShot: Knife dicing onion into tiny pieces.
steps.watchOut: Big chunks, which make the bhel hard to eat and spoil the crunch balance; and juicy tomato pulp, which makes it soggy, so scoop out the watery seeds and use only the firm flesh.

steps.title: Dice the potato
steps.text: Peel the cooled boiled potato and dice 40 g into small cubes.
steps.visualCue: Small, soft yellow cubes that hold their shape
steps.cameraCheck: The diced potato on the board
steps.watchOut: Warm potato, which wilts the sev and puffed rice; let it cool to room temperature first.

steps.title: Crush the papdi
steps.text: Break 2 papdi (10 g) into small pieces by hand.
steps.visualCue: Irregular, crisp pieces the size of a thumbnail
steps.cameraCheck: The broken papdi in a bowl
steps.watchOut: Papdi that bends instead of snapping, which means it has gone soft; crisp it in a dry pan for 30 sec on low heat or use fresh ones.

steps.title: Combine the bhel base
steps.text: In a large bowl add the toasted puffed rice, 30 g onion, 30 g tomato, 40 g potato, the chopped chilli and 8 g roasted peanuts. Toss gently.
steps.visualCue: Vegetables spread evenly through the puffs, which are still dry and loose
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl of dry mixed bhel
steps.videoShot: Spoon folding puffed rice and vegetables.
steps.watchOut: Heavy stirring that crushes the puffs into dust; lift and fold from the bottom instead.

steps.title: Add the chutneys and seasoning
steps.text: Spoon in 15 g tamarind chutney and 10 g green chutney, then add 1 g chaat masala, 0.5 g salt and 5 ml lemon juice. Toss quickly.
steps.tip: Taste one puff: it should be sweet, sour and spicy in turns; fix with a squeeze of lemon (sour), chutney (sweet) or chilli.
steps.visualCue: Puffs coated in a light brown-green film, still separate and crunchy, with a sharp, tangy smell
steps.cameraCheck: The coated bhel in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Chutneys drizzled and tossed through the puffed rice.
steps.watchOut: Over-mixing or leaving it to sit, which turns the puffs soggy within minutes; toss in 8–10 quick folds and stop. If it is too dry or too bland, add 1 tsp chutney, not water.

steps.title: Add papdi and half the sev
steps.text: Add the crushed papdi and 5 g of the 10 g sev. Give 2–3 gentle folds.
steps.visualCue: Crisp pieces of papdi and sev visible all through the bhel
steps.cameraCheck: The bhel with papdi and sev in it
steps.videoShot: Crushed papdi and sev falling into the bowl.
steps.watchOut: Mixing them in early so they go soft; they go in last so they stay crisp.

steps.title: Plate and top
steps.text: Tip onto a plate or a paper cone. Top with the remaining 5 g sev and 4 g chopped coriander. Eat straight away.
steps.visualCue: A loose, crunchy heap with golden sev on top and green flecks, with a tangy, spicy smell
steps.videoShot: A spoon lifting a crunchy forkful of bhel.
steps.watchOut: Waiting; it loses its crunch in about 5 minutes (est.), so eat it as soon as it is plated. A soggy plate cannot be rescued except by adding fresh sev and puffed rice on top.
steps.funFact: Bhel is closely linked to Mumbai's beaches, especially Chowpatty and Juhu (Wikipedia, via DBpedia mirror).

reasons: no frying at home (the fried sev and papdi are bought), low saturated fat (about 2.5 g) and no cholesterol, plus raw vegetables and peanuts for crunch and some protein. Points off because most of it is refined puffed rice and fried crunch with only about 5 g fibre and 9 g protein, about 5 g added sugar from the sweet chutney, and sodium of about 520 mg (est.). Restaurant versions usually use more sev, sweet chutney, salt and sometimes cheese, with fewer vegetables, so they are heavier and saltier (est.).

researchRating.basis: one of the best-known Indian street snacks, carried by almost every major recipe site and described as Mumbai's most popular street food. Points off because the recipe pages could not be opened here, so star counts and reviews could not be read, and because it only works fresh, which is a common complaint with home and delivered versions. The number is an estimate from how widely and warmly it is covered.

storage: Do not store the mixed bhel; the puffed rice and sev go soft quickly. Store the parts separately: puffed rice, sev and papdi in an airtight container at room temperature; chopped onion and tomato in the fridge for about 1 day (est.); chutneys in a clean closed jar in the fridge for several days (est., not sourced). Freezing the mixed bhel is not recommended. No reheating; if you have to, do not.
leftoverRemix: Bhel stuffed cucumber cups or bhel on toast. If a little mixed bhel is left and still crisp enough, scoop it into hollowed cucumber slices and top with fresh sev. Or use the leftover chutneys in a sandwich or on a chaat plate.
burnOff: about 4.9 km of running (340 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 6.8 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 20 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: puffed rice is a rice (grain) product and the recipe uses onion, chaat masala and table salt, which the common rule set avoids (it allows sabudana, kuttu, singhara, sendha namak). Assumption: the common North and West India rule set.

ekadashi.reason: puffed rice is a grain, avoided on Ekadashi under the common rule set, and the recipe also has onion.

jain.reason: drop the onion and potato and use cucumber or capsicum and boiled raw banana; no garlic in the chutney; check sev and papdi labels.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; light and quick for iftar. Not a good sehri on its own: protein is only about 9 g (est.) and it is fairly salty.

jain.reason: the main recipe uses onion and potato (roots); swap onion for cucumber or capsicum and potato for boiled raw banana, and skip garlic, as in the Jain variant. Check that bought sev and papdi are made without onion or garlic.

vegan.reason: puffed rice, sev, papdi, vegetables, peanuts and jaggery-tamarind chutney contain no dairy, ghee, honey or egg.

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: leave out the 30 g onion (use cucumber or capsicum); garlic is not in the recipe, but many street green chutneys add it, so skip it in the chutney.

glutenFree.reason: the papdi is made from refined wheat flour (maida). Use the Gluten-free variant (skip papdi), and check that bought sev is besan-only and that chaat masala has no hing, because most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour.

dairyFree.reason: no milk, curd, ghee, paneer or cheese in the main recipe. (Some stalls sell "cheese bhel"; that is not this recipe.)

variants.name: Jain Bhel (no onion, potato or garlic)
